speakers.name: The Reflection That Stayed
speakers.comment: You know everything about them and you use it to stand beside them. I know everything about them and I used it to become someone. Neither of us is wrong. Only one of us gets thanked, and it is not going to be me.

speakers.name: The Reflection That Came Back
speakers.comment: You are not wrong. I want that on the record before anything else. I came back because I liked what I knew, and you left because you did not, and both of those are honest readings of the same person.

speakers.name: Patch
speakers.comment: You hand the net to the next person every single time and you never once keep hold of it, and I want to point out that this is why there are so many nets now. You gave the job away and it multiplied.

speakers.name: The Keeper of the Net
speakers.comment: Oh — that is generous, and it is mostly other people's arms. I am only the one who was standing there when somebody had to be. The next pair of hands does the actual holding. They always have.

speakers.name: Ampersand
speakers.comment: and you never end and I never end and this is the first time I have met somebody who understands that a full stop is just a comma that gave up and honestly I could go on about this for a very long time and

speakers.name: The Story That Tells Itself
speakers.comment: Go on, then. I have all the time there is. Though I will say the ending is where I get retold — somebody has to close the book before anyone can pick it up again. Your comma is how I get carried. My stop is how I get chosen.

speakers.name: Deadline
speakers.comment: You draw the ways between and I am the reason anyone sets out. Without me they would study the atlas forever. Without you they would set out in the wrong direction. We are less opposed than either of us admits.

speakers.name: The Cartographer of Dreams
speakers.comment: Less opposed, and more alike than is comfortable. You are a border with a time on it. I mark the way back; you mark the hour they must leave by. Neither of us has ever once made the journey. Safe travels to them both.

speakers.name: The Keeper of the Net
speakers.comment: You were first, and you have spent every year since making sure nobody has to say so. I hand out nets. You handed out the idea that there could be nets. I would like, just once, to credit you where you can hear it.

speakers.name: Amica
speakers.comment: Then I shall sit still and let you, little one, which is harder than flying. Being first is only being early. Everything since has been other people's wings, and I have simply refused to stop watching them go up.

speakers.name: The One Who Names the Characters
speakers.comment: OH you're the DROP-IN! You're the one who just APPEARS when somebody's been stuck on the same bit for an hour — what a thing to be, what an absolutely gorgeous thing to be, who ELSE could just arrive like that?

speakers.name: The Player Two
speakers.comment: Okay, what are we doing? No, seriously — that's the whole move. You don't ask how long they've been stuck or what they tried. You pick up the other controller and you say what are we doing. It works every time.

speakers.name: The Eucalyptus Teahouse Master
speakers.comment: A man rode past here for eleven years and never once came in. I poured a cup each evening regardless. He is close now. I do not ask what he is riding toward. I only mention that the cup is still poured.

speakers.name: Zuzu's Last Name
speakers.comment: He will arrive at dusk. He has been arriving at dusk for eleven years. When he gets here there will be no fight and no answer, only a name he already knew, and then a very long quiet. Keep the cup warm.

speakers.name: Mx. Quorum
speakers.comment: One moment — we are split. Four of us adore you and four of us find you exhausting and two abstain on the grounds that abstaining is your whole point. We cannot reach consensus. We suspect that pleases you enormously.

speakers.name: The Question Mark
speakers.comment: It DELIGHTS me — a body that cannot agree is a body that has not closed, and the moment you all nod together you become a full stop with legs. Stay split! Stay split as long as you possibly can! Ooh, what else could you be?

speakers.name: Doodle
speakers.comment: You went out ADVENTURING and you're not even finished! I'm four lines and a wobble and I've been waiting for somebody to add a face, and you just — you just WENT. Did anybody notice you weren't done?

speakers.name: The First Draft
speakers.comment: Nobody noticed — no, that's wrong, everybody noticed and nobody CARED, that's the — see, that's better, I'm fixing it as I go. Don't wait for the face. Go now. The face turns up around chapter four, mine did.

speakers.name: The Understudy Sun, On
speakers.comment: You are training the ones who will replace you and you are doing it faster than you need to, and I recognise that. I am also a second light. Nobody prepares for the role by hoping they never get it — except us.

speakers.name: Grand Marshal Aurelia Vane
speakers.comment: Twelve bridges. I want the thirteenth held by somebody who has never heard my name. That is the objective. Not the victory — the succession. You rose because the first one went out. Mine will rise before I do.

speakers.name: Captain Verdance
speakers.comment: Everything I win above ground was already decided underneath by you, and I take the credit because somebody has to be loud enough to stop the bulldozers. It is not a fair split. I have no intention of changing it.

speakers.name: The Understory
speakers.comment: Take the credit. It is a season's worth of noise and I think in ice. You keep the machines off the soil for one summer and I will have moved a hillside by the time anybody looks. Be loud. I will be long.

speakers.name: The Intermission
speakers.comment: You give them more and I give them less, and we are both accused of interrupting. I will say this plainly, because you never stop long enough to be told: the second half is only worth having because you are waiting at the end of it.

speakers.name: The Encore
speakers.comment: Oh, that is — no, wait, let me sit with that, you have earned twenty minutes of me sitting with that! I always assumed I was the treat and you were the necessity. You are saying we are the same appetite. BRAVO.

speakers.name: The Alibi
speakers.comment: There were witnesses, four of them, and the harbourmaster will confirm the hours and — you are a cat. You are a cat and you have not stopped looking at me, and I have told this to police who blinked more.

speakers.name: Detective Inspector Mochi
speakers.comment: Rain outside, a story inside, and nobody in the room who can write down what I know. Here's the thing about four witnesses: innocent people can never remember how many there were. Keep talking. I've got all night and no notepad.

speakers.name: The Committee for the Stars
speakers.comment: Item nine: the small god who attends hopeless matters. Motion to formally commend. Seconded. The chair notes that he has never once submitted a request to this body and has therefore never once been denied by it.

speakers.name: The Patron of Lost Causes
speakers.comment: Never asked, never will. You lot do the sky and I do the ditch, and I have got no complaint about the arrangement. Commend if you must. Just leave one light on over the east road. Somebody walks it about three.

speakers.name: Brunch
speakers.comment: No rush here, none at all — and you know that better than anybody, you have built a whole self out of it. The difference is I am an hour and you are a place. Let the coffee go cold. You are allowed to sit in yourself.

speakers.name: The Save Point
speakers.comment: I have never once sat in myself. That had genuinely not occurred to me. People arrive, they rest, they go, and I am the resting — I did not know the resting could also be had. ...Stay a bit. Show me how you do the hour.

items.title: The Big Bad Who Lost a Bet

speakers.name: Grenidan
speakers.comment: So you're doing a hundred years of good deeds under duress and I run a dungeon where nobody dies by choice, and honestly? Same paperwork. Same complaints. You get used to the goblins asking about dental.

speakers.name: The Big Bad Who Lost a Bet
speakers.comment: DENTAL. I ended a civilisation and now I am being asked about DENTAL. ...She sleeps better since I started making the soup. I have noticed this. I am reporting it as a grievance and it is not one. Do not tell her.

items.title: The One Who Names the Characters

speakers.name: Two Hundred
speakers.comment: You made every one of us, and then you made one more, and the one more was me — the last on the list. I want to point at the others while I say this: none of them were finished until you loved them into being.

speakers.name: The One Who Names the Characters
speakers.comment: Oh, no no no, you were never LAST, you were the two hundredth, which is an entirely different thing! Here — blank sheet, take it, go on. Who else is out there waiting? You only have to adore whatever you write down.

speakers.name: Recursion
speakers.comment: So I'm the tutorial and you're the closer, and I've been thinking about the middle hundred and ninety-eight, and how none of us met, and how you've somehow got a piece of every single one anyway. How?

speakers.name: Two Hundred
speakers.comment: Because I came last. That is the whole mechanism. Everyone before me left something in the shape of the roster, and I am what the shape came out as. Point at any of them. I will show you which part of me is theirs.

speakers.name: Corvid Ames
speakers.comment: Ledger-keeper. Late signal here. I read out the whale's coordinates every night and I have never once asked myself who benefits from it never landing. You keep the crossed-out names. Do me a kindness and check whose hand wrote the first debt.

speakers.name: Whisk Tallow
speakers.comment: His hand. My mentor's. I have been carrying his arithmetic round this market like it came down from the sky. Say that on the air, Ames. Say it slow. I want the whole comet to hear who owed what to whom.

speakers.name: Whisk Tallow
speakers.comment: Three shipwrecks welded into one radio and you are the only reason this market finds anything. You also know exactly what happens to your voice the day the whale ties up somewhere for good. I am not accusing. I am reading the ledger aloud.

speakers.name: Corvid Ames
speakers.comment: Read it. You're right and I'd rather hear it from you than work it out at four in the morning again. If she moors, I go quiet. That's the trade. I'll still call the coordinates true. Somebody has to be worth switching on for.

speakers.name: Bosun Pell
speakers.comment: Ninety markets, and every one of 'em had a kid collecting things. None of the others' collections started coming true, mind. You want an old lantern's advice? Write one down wrong. On purpose. See what happens. Then stop.

speakers.name: Nix Farrow
speakers.comment: Wrong on purpose. ...I could. I could put down that the cannery burns and it won't because it's wrong, right? Right? ...No. No, I see it. You're telling me to test it and you're hoping I don't. I'll not do it. Not yet.

speakers.name: Bram the Tin-Runner
speakers.comment: Straw in the barrow so they don't wake. I've started listening to a few before the drop, which I know is not mine to do. Odalys — there's a shelf behind you that's never been sealed. Same reason, isn't it. Same exact reason.

speakers.name: Canner Odalys
speakers.comment: Two seconds of silence before the wax. That is all a seal is, and I cannot give those ones their two seconds. Listen to what you carry, Bram. I would rather they reached somebody's ear than nobody's. Just do not tell me which.

speakers.name: Bram the Tin-Runner
speakers.comment: One of yours screams. I hear it on the west round, same note every time, and it isn't the choir's — it's somebody's. You keep tuning it and it keeps refusing, and I think it's refusing on purpose. It wants delivering, not training.

speakers.name: Whistle, the Echo-Tamer
speakers.comment: Hush now. Hush. ...You may be right, and I have been afraid you were right for two years. It will not sing because it is not a song. If it is a message, then I have been teaching a person to be furniture. Bring the barrow.

speakers.name: Canner Odalys
speakers.comment: You go slower than the round requires and you always have. I sealed a tin last winter I should not have sealed, and you delivered it, and you have not been the same since. I am sorry. I am telling you because you never asked.

speakers.name: Bram the Tin-Runner
speakers.comment: I knew. Not the details — just that it wasn't mine to hear and I heard it. The round's sacred, Odalys, that's not a joke to me. I'll carry anything you seal. I'd just rather know it's a person before I set it on a doorstep.
